metadata.description: Partial folder names skipped during CLF processing. Matched as a CASE-SENSITIVE SUBSTRING of the folder name with spaces replaced by underscores (see should_skip_folder in src/utils/myfuncs/file_utils.py), so each casing needs its own entry.
metadata.usage: Match these patterns against folder names to determine if a folder should be skipped during CLF processing
rules: NEVER put a MATERIAL or ALLOY name in this list. It names what a part is made of, not what the part IS, so it removes solid geometry. The pattern 'ebm-ti64' did exactly that: it silently excluded 52 Solid_CORE/Solid_SKIN folders across 11 plates - including every tensile specimen (ten-ebm-ti64-*) on build 512002, which is named 'EBM04 Tensile Failure Build'. Removed in v1.4.
Only exclude what is not part surface we want defects on: supports, porous structure, labels.

An excluded folder can be the ONLY geometry at a height, and that layer is then written as an empty []. Part 201 has 300 such layers of 3021, so a path-layer FILE count overstates the drawn layers - count non-empty layers instead.
Removing a pattern can promote another to load-bearing: 'porous' had 0 unique hits only because 'ebm-ti64' also matched those folders.

v1.5: added lowercase 'support'. 36 folders named *_Contour_support and *_Peg_Contour_support were being EXTRACTED because the list held 'Support', 'supports' and 'SUPPORTS' but not the bare lowercase word, and matching is case-sensitive. Their contours are 22 points with a median segment of 0.039mm and ONE segment of 49.2mm - a support outline, not a part - and that 49mm chord is the long diagonal drawn across every part on build 512002's overlays, filled into the cut mask as if it were metal.

changelog.1.4: Removed 'ebm-ti64' (excluded real solid parts). Added 'POROUS' for casing symmetry with 'SUPPORTS'. Dropped '_Support' and 'Supports' as strict substrings of 'Support'. Net effect measured over 1137 folders on 11 plates: 52 folders newly included, all core/skin; 0 newly excluded; 0 support/porous folders promoted.
